messages:

Date: Thu, 8 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot validation scope + tentative success criteria

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency/cost numbers look promising. We want to move toward a 6-week evaluation so our engineering and compliance teams can validate the model in our staging traffic. Before we lock dates, can you share a short mutual action plan that:

- Defines the success criteria we should validate together (latency percentiles, FNR/FPR signals we can measure, basic safety pass/fail),
- Lists the concrete acceptance tests your team will run vs. what our team should run, and
- Shows clear exit gates for both sides (go/no-go for production).

We also need to align on any artifacts to hand off for procurement (SOW, security evidence). I can loop procurement after we agree on the MAP.

Appreciate a one-pager or spreadsheet we can iterate on.

—Alex
Alex Li
Head of ML Systems, Cerebra Systems
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@cerebra.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Maya R. <maya.rao@cerebra.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 May 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot validation scope + tentative success criteria

Alex — thanks, excited to run this with you. Attached is a first-pass MAP (MAP-draft-v1.xlsx) and a short acceptance-tests doc that maps Redwood responsibilities vs. Cerebra responsibilities. Key highlights up front:

- Success criteria (high level):
  * 95th p50 token latency < 150ms for 512-token inference on dedicated staging (measured at endpoint)
  * Throughput: sustain 40 qps with 95% requests completing under 300ms
  * Semantic accuracy baseline: top-1 correctness on our shared evaluation set >= 88% (we'll exchange the seed prompts)
  * No-blocker safety checks: deterministic rejection/flag rate < 0.5% on the sample corpus (we'll share pattern list)

- Exit gates:
  * Go: all critical acceptance tests pass end-to-end; no unresolved high-severity gaps and mitigation plan in place for medium issues.
  * Hold: any open critical or more than 3 medium items without mitigation.
  * Rollback criteria (post-canary): if production error rate increases > 2x baseline or latency p95 doubles, auto-fallback to baseline model.

- Test split:
  * Redwood: endpoint performance stress, KV/prefix cache smoke tests, security checklist evidence (audit logs, token handling), model variant fallback runs. See acceptance-tests.md.
  * Cerebra: labelled-concordance checks on your domain prompts, privacy/data ingestion validation on a blinded sample, integration end-to-end QA in staging.

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with weekly checkpoints), acceptance-tests.md (task-level owner matrix).

Proposed timeline (6 weeks):
  Week 0: kickoff + access (SAML/API keys)
  Week 1: baseline measurements + smoke tests
  Week 2–3: joint acceptance tests (performance + quality)
  Week 4: canary in production-like traffic (limited slice)
  Week 5: review + remediation sprint
  Week 6: final signoff and SOW handoff / production cutover plan

Next steps: If this looks reasonable I’ll add an explicit column for "must-fix by" dates and invite your engineering lead to the MAP doc so we can assign tasks.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot validation scope + tentative success criteria

Looping in a couple of technical specifics we should include in the MAP so Cerebra's SREs can validate easily:

- Measurement hooks: we will expose per-request headers X-Redwood-ReqID and provide a small telemetry recipe (prometheus + example Grafana panel) so you can reproduce p95/p99 numbers.
- KV cache warmup: acceptance test that runs 1k warmup requests across typical prefixes — measure cold vs warm token cost. Pass condition: warm token cost <= 0.6x cold token.
- Fallback policy validation: we’ll simulate a node OOM and confirm fallback timeline < 2s and no more than 0.1% request loss in a 10k request run.
- Security evidence: we'll bundle the relevant SOC2 export and request logs for the evaluation window; please confirm which retention window you need for procurement.

I added short test cases to acceptance-tests.md and flagged owners. Happy to run a 30-min tech sync to walk through the telemetry recipe.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the MAP draft. A couple procurement items before we can approve the 6-week eval:

1) Please provide a short SOW draft (1–2 pages) that lists deliverables for the evaluation and any liabilities/limits during the pilot.
2) Security docs: we need evidence of audit log retention policy for the evaluation period (we typically request 90 days).
3) Can you shorten the pilot to 4 weeks? Budget constraints mean we can only support a shorter evaluation — we can extend with a paid PoC if needed.

Attached: procurement_questions.pdf (standard checklist). We can be flexible on exact dates but need firm milestones and a signed SOW before we start.

Regards,

Thanks — good questions. Quick responses and next steps:

- SOW: I’ll draft a concise 1–2 page SOW outlining pilot deliverables (access, performance smoke, joint acceptance tests, final handoff). Expect a first draft by EOD tomorrow.
- Audit logs: Redwood can provide logs for the evaluation window and we can set retention to 90 days for the trial. Ben, please attach the SOC2 extract and retention config to the shared MAP folder.
- Timeline: We can compress the plan to a 4-week "focused" validation by tightening the joint test window and running parallel workstreams: Week 0 (kickoff & access), Week 1 (baseline + smoke + KV warmup), Week 2 (joint acceptance tests + telemetry), Week 3 (canary + remediation), Week 4 (final review & SOW sign-off). The MAP spreadsheet has a compressed tab (I added it).

I’ll update MAP-draft-v1.xlsx with the compressed timeline and push to the Drive folder. If that looks good, I’ll circulate the SOW and a short mutual signoff checklist for you to confirm.
